items.title: The Stealth AI Stocks Are Dragging Down the Dow Again
items.summary: Caterpillar and Goldman Sachs are two of the biggest stocks in the Dow.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 50 points, or 0.1%, on a day when 22 of its 30 members were actually rising.  Chip stocks were getting hammered after a big run, fitting into a pattern of two-way volatility that’s characterized the group’s moves all year.

items.title: Goldman Sachs Bulks Up Asset Management Business With LCN Deal
items.summary: Goldman Sachs struck its second deal in a week as the firm pushes ahead with plans to grow its $4 trillion money-management arm. The company will pay as much as $410 million to buy LCN Capital Partners, a commercial real estate investor that focuses on sale-leaseback agreements and triple-net leases. Todd Gillespie has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest."

items.title: Goldman Sachs Agrees Deal to Buy LCN Capital Partners for Up to $410 Million
items.summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc (NYSE:GS) has agreed to acquire real estate investment manager LCN Capital Partners in a transaction potentially worth as much as $410 million, expanding its capabilities in sale-leaseback, build-to-suit and triple net lease investments. LCN managed approximately $3 billion in assets as of June 30, 2026 and operates across North America and Europe, combining expertise in corporate credit with real estate investing.

items.title: Goldman Sachs to Buy Real-Estate Investment Firm for Up to $410 Million
items.summary: LCN Capital Partners specializes in sale-leaseback transactions and manages about $3 billion in assets.

items.title: ByteDance Draws Over $30 Billion in Orders for Jumbo Bank Loan
items.summary: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has attracted more than $30 billion of orders for its jumbo syndicated loan, people familiar with the matter said, indicating strong interest from lenders as the Chinese technology giant ramps up investments in artificial intelligence.

items.title: Goldman Sachs acquires LCN Capital Partners for up to $410 million
items.summary: The deal includes $260 million upfront and up to $150 million more tied to performance targets, with about 80% paid in stock

items.title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Just Backed A $1 Billion Reinsurance Sidecar In Bermuda
items.summary: Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE: GS) and Talcott Financial Group partnered to launch West Grove Re, a Bermuda based US$1b reinsurance sidecar. Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management will act as investment manager for West Grove Re, focusing on private asset strategies. The vehicle is intended to provide capital efficient solutions for insurance liabilities and to expand Goldman Sachs exposure to insurance and reinsurance markets. Consider looking across other insurers and asset managers involved...
